tuiuiu.description: Large wading bird, symbol of the Pantanal, frequently observed in open and flooded areas.
tuiuiu.physicalCharacteristics: White plumage, black head and red crop, with long legs and a robust beak.
tuiuiu.habitat: Floodable fields, bays, ebbs and river banks.
tuiuiu.behavior: It builds tall nests and can be seen foraging in shallow waters.
tuiuiu.diet: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, insects and small vertebrates.
curiosities: It is one of the largest flying birds in South America.
Your nest can be reused for several years.
tuiuiu.distribution: Central and South America, including the entire Pantanal.
tuiuiu.ecologicalImportance: Helps indicate food availability and health of wetlands.

arara-azul.description: Large macaw, recognized by its cobalt blue plumage and powerful beak.
arara-azul.physicalCharacteristics: Intense blue, yellow ring around the eyes and base of the beak.
arara-azul.habitat: Riparian forests, carandazal areas and forest edges.
arara-azul.behavior: It lives in pairs or family groups and uses hollow trees to nest.
arara-azul.diet: Mainly palm fruit, such as acuri and bocaiúva.
curiosities: The beak breaks very resistant fruits.
Conservation depends on the supply of palm trees and hollow trees.
arara-azul.distribution: Central Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay, with an important population in the Pantanal.
arara-azul.ecologicalImportance: It disperses seeds and participates in the regeneration of Pantanal palm trees.

onca-pintada.description: Largest feline in the Americas and top predator in swamp environments.
onca-pintada.physicalCharacteristics: Golden coat with rosettes, muscular body and very powerful bite.
onca-pintada.habitat: Forests close to rivers, streams and areas with a good supply of prey.
onca-pintada.diet: Capybaras, alligators, peccaries, deer and other vertebrates.
curiosities: The rosettes may have small central dots.
Rivers and bays are important corridors for the species.
onca-pintada.distribution: From Mexico to northern Argentina, with a relevant population in the Pantanal.
onca-pintada.ecologicalImportance: Regulates prey populations and helps maintain balance in food chains.

capivara.description: Largest living rodent in the world, closely associated with the banks of bodies of water.
capivara.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, partially webbed paws and reddish-brown fur.
capivara.habitat: Banks of rivers, lagoons, bays and humid fields.
capivara.behavior: Social, lives in groups and seeks refuge in the water when threatened.
curiosities: It can remain submerged for several minutes.
Groups tend to have strong social organization.
capivara.distribution: Much of South America, including the Pantanal.
capivara.ecologicalImportance: It is important prey for large predators and influences the vegetation on the banks.

jacare-do-pantanal.description: Alligator abundant in the Pantanal waters, adapted to the seasonal dynamics of floods.
jacare-do-pantanal.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, narrow snout and light bands on the jaw.
jacare-do-pantanal.habitat: Bays, streams, lagoons and slow-moving rivers.
jacare-do-pantanal.behavior: It sunbathes on the banks and hunts mainly during the nocturnal activity period.
jacare-do-pantanal.diet: Fish, crustaceans, amphibians and small vertebrates.
curiosities: Wetlands provide shelter and food during droughts.
Cubs use marginal vegetation for protection.
jacare-do-pantanal.distribution: Central South America, especially Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay.
jacare-do-pantanal.ecologicalImportance: It participates in the control of aquatic populations and transports nutrients between water and banks.

anta.description: Large herbivorous mammal that roams forests, paths and riverbanks in the Pantanal.
anta.physicalCharacteristics: Bulky body, elongated snout and short brown fur.
anta.habitat: Riparian forests, capons and areas close to water.
anta.behavior: Solitary, generally more active at dusk and at night.
anta.diet: Leaves, fruits, shoots and other parts of plants.
curiosities: It is an important seed disperser.
It swims well and uses water to escape threats.
anta.distribution: South America east of the Andes, including the Pantanal.
anta.ecologicalImportance: It transports seeds between different environments and contributes to forest regeneration.

tamandua-bandeira.description: Mammal specialized in capturing ants and termites with its long, sticky tongue.
tamandua-bandeira.physicalCharacteristics: Tubular snout, very voluminous tail and dark diagonal stripe on the body.
tamandua-bandeira.habitat: Fields, savannas and forest edges with soil suitable for digging.
tamandua-bandeira.behavior: It walks long distances and can be active day or night.
curiosities: It has no functional teeth.
The tongue can be repeatedly projected to remove insects from nests.
tamandua-bandeira.distribution: Central and South America, including open areas of the Pantanal.
tamandua-bandeira.ecologicalImportance: Controls populations of social insects and turns the soil by opening anthills and termite mounds.

cervo-do-pantanal.description: Largest deer in South America, associated with floodplains, swamps and floodable fields.
cervo-do-pantanal.physicalCharacteristics: Long legs, reddish-brown fur and branched antlers in males.
cervo-do-pantanal.habitat: Swamps, bays, floodable fields and river banks.
cervo-do-pantanal.behavior: It uses flooded areas as shelter and moves in search of aquatic vegetation.
cervo-do-pantanal.diet: Grasses, aquatic plants, leaves and shoots.
curiosities: Leg adaptations favor movement on damp terrain.
The species depends on maintaining connected wetlands.
cervo-do-pantanal.distribution: Central and southern South America, occurring in the Pantanal.
cervo-do-pantanal.ecologicalImportance: It participates in the dynamics of wetland vegetation and disperses seeds.

ema.description: Large running bird that occupies fields and open areas of the Pantanal.
ema.physicalCharacteristics: Long neck, reduced wings, strong legs and brown plumage.
ema.habitat: Fields, savannas and open areas with low vegetation.
ema.behavior: It lives in groups and runs quickly when disturbed.
ema.diet: Fruits, seeds, leaves and small animals.
curiosities: The male participates in incubating and caring for the young.
The wings help with balance while running.
ema.distribution: South America, occurring in open areas of the Pantanal.
ema.ecologicalImportance: It disperses seeds and integrates the food chains of the fields.

colhereiro.description: Aquatic bird with a spatulate bill, observed in shallow waters and muddy banks.
colhereiro.physicalCharacteristics: Pink plumage, light neck and long beak with a spoon-shaped tip.
colhereiro.habitat: Lagoons, bays, marshes and river banks.
colhereiro.behavior: Moves its beak from side to side in the water to locate food.
colhereiro.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, insects and other aquatic invertebrates.
curiosities: The pink color is related to food.
It usually forages in groups in shallow areas.
colhereiro.distribution: Americas, mainly coastal and continental wetlands.
colhereiro.ecologicalImportance: Connects the food chains of invertebrates and small fish in wetlands.

garca-branca.description: Large, pale heron, common on banks, floodplains and bodies of water in the Pantanal.
garca-branca.physicalCharacteristics: White plumage, long neck, yellow beak and dark legs.
garca-branca.habitat: Rivers, bays, streams, swamps and flooded fields.
garca-branca.behavior: It walks slowly in shallow water and captures prey with a quick swipe of its beak.
garca-branca.diet: Fish, amphibians, small reptiles, crustaceans and insects.
curiosities: It can remain motionless for long periods while hunting.
It gathers in colonies for reproduction.
garca-branca.distribution: Wide worldwide distribution, with presence throughout Brazil.
garca-branca.ecologicalImportance: It preys on several aquatic organisms and indicates the availability of food on the banks.

sucuri-verde.description: Large semi-aquatic snake that uses rivers, bays and flooded areas to hunt.
sucuri-verde.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, olive green color with dark spots and eyes positioned on top of the head.
sucuri-verde.habitat: Swamps, lagoons, bays, streams and river banks.
sucuri-verde.behavior: It remains partially submerged and captures prey by constriction.
sucuri-verde.diet: Fish, birds, mammals and other vertebrates of compatible size.
curiosities: The nostrils and eyes help to observe the surroundings with the body submerged.
It is one of the largest snakes in the world by body mass.
sucuri-verde.distribution: Tropical regions of South America, including the Pantanal.
sucuri-verde.ecologicalImportance: It acts as a top predator in aquatic and riverine environments.

jabuti-piranga.description: Terrestrial tortoise with predominantly diurnal habits, found in forested areas and their surroundings.
jabuti-piranga.physicalCharacteristics: Dark carapace with yellow or orange spots and colored scales on the legs.
jabuti-piranga.habitat: Forests, thickets, forest edges and areas with litter.
jabuti-piranga.behavior: It moves along the ground and looks for food among fallen leaves and fruits.
jabuti-piranga.diet: Fruits, leaves, flowers, fungi and small invertebrates.
curiosities: It can contribute to the dispersal of seeds from fruits it consumes.
The shell offers protection, but does not make the species immune to fires and habitat loss.
jabuti-piranga.distribution: North and central South America, including areas of central Brazil.
jabuti-piranga.ecologicalImportance: It disperses seeds and participates in the cycling of organic matter in the soil.

sapo-cururu.description: Large frog, adaptable to open areas and frequently observed after rain.
sapo-cururu.physicalCharacteristics: Rough skin, evident parotoid glands and variable coloration in earthy tones.
sapo-cururu.habitat: Fields, forest edges, temporary wetlands and modified environments.
sapo-cururu.behavior: It is most active at night and breeds in temporary or permanent bodies of water.
curiosities: Skin glands produce defensive substances.
Tadpoles depend on water to complete their development.
sapo-cururu.distribution: Central Brazil and other areas of South America, including the Pantanal.
sapo-cururu.ecologicalImportance: It controls invertebrates and serves as food for predators.

ra-pimenta.description: Large frog associated with humid areas, puddles and vegetated banks.
ra-pimenta.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, brown back with contrasting designs and strong hind limbs.
ra-pimenta.habitat: Swamps, temporary ponds, wet fields and stream banks.
ra-pimenta.behavior: It can build foam nests and vocalizes mainly during the reproductive period.
ra-pimenta.diet: Insects, spiders and other small animals.
curiosities: The foam helps protect eggs in environments subject to fluctuations in water levels.
The species is known for strong vocalizations during rains.
ra-pimenta.distribution: Brazil and neighboring countries, occurring in open and humid areas of the center-south.
ra-pimenta.ecologicalImportance: It participates in the control of invertebrates and is sensitive to changes in reproductive areas.

pintado.description: Large leather fish, important in rivers and in traditional fishing in the Pantanal.
pintado.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, flat head, wattles and dark striped spots.
pintado.habitat: River channels, wells and sections with currents.
pintado.behavior: Active predator, especially when locating moving fish.
curiosities: The wattles help in perceiving the environment.
Reproduction follows the pulse of floods and migration through rivers.
pintado.distribution: Paraná-Paraguay and São Francisco basins, including the Pantanal.
pintado.ecologicalImportance: It is a relevant predator and an indicator of the connectivity of river environments.

pacu.description: Frugivorous and omnivorous fish that uses rivers, bays and flooded areas of the Pantanal.
pacu.physicalCharacteristics: High and compressed body, strong teeth and silver to dark color.
pacu.habitat: Rivers, bays, streams and forests flooded during floods.
pacu.behavior: It forms schools and exploits fruits and seeds that fall into the water.
pacu.diet: Fruits, seeds, plants, algae and small animals.
curiosities: The flood connects feeding and breeding areas.
Can disperse seeds of riverine plants.
pacu.distribution: Paraguay Basin and other basins in South America.
pacu.ecologicalImportance: Transports seeds and energy between flooded terrestrial environments and rivers.

piraputanga.description: Agile freshwater fish, associated with fast-flowing rivers and environments connected by floods.
piraputanga.physicalCharacteristics: Silver body, dark back, colorful fins and mouth adapted to various items.
piraputanga.habitat: Rivers, streams, streams and riparian forest areas.
piraputanga.behavior: It swims in schools and looks for food in the water column and near the banks.
piraputanga.diet: Fruits, seeds, insects and small fish.
curiosities: The riparian forest provides fruit and shade for aquatic environments.
Coloration may become more intense during reproductive periods.
piraputanga.ecologicalImportance: Connects plant production from the banks to aquatic chains and disperses seeds.

caranguejo-agua-doce.description: Freshwater crab found in lentic environments and river banks in the Paraguay basin.
caranguejo-agua-doce.physicalCharacteristics: Flat carapace, developed pincers and brown to reddish color.
caranguejo-agua-doce.habitat: Lagoons, bays, streams, banks and aquatic vegetation.
caranguejo-agua-doce.behavior: It uses the bottom and vegetation to look for food and shelter.
caranguejo-agua-doce.diet: Debris, algae, plant matter and small organisms.
curiosities: The species participates in the decomposition of aquatic organic matter.
Shelter availability varies with flood and drought.
caranguejo-agua-doce.distribution: Inland basins of South America, including the Paraguay basin.
caranguejo-agua-doce.ecologicalImportance: It recycles organic matter and serves as food for fish and waterfowl.

camarao-agua-doce.description: Freshwater shrimp associated with rivers, lakes and floodable areas in several Brazilian basins.
camarao-agua-doce.physicalCharacteristics: Segmented body, elongated rostrum and first pair of chelae developed.
camarao-agua-doce.habitat: Rivers, lagoons, bays and areas of aquatic vegetation.
camarao-agua-doce.behavior: It searches for food at the bottom and among plants, with variable activity throughout the day.
camarao-agua-doce.diet: Debris, algae, small invertebrates and organic matter.
curiosities: The life cycle can use fresh waters and environments with higher salinity in different populations.
It is a relevant species for food chains and riverside communities.
camarao-agua-doce.distribution: Wide distribution in South America, with records in Brazilian basins.
camarao-agua-doce.ecologicalImportance: Transfers energy from debris and vegetation to fish and waterfowl.

bugio-preto.description: Primate with a powerful vocalization, associated with riparian forests and grasslands in the Pantanal.
bugio-preto.physicalCharacteristics: Dark coat in males, marked face and prehensile tail.
bugio-preto.habitat: Riparian forests, thickets and forest edges.
bugio-preto.behavior: It lives in groups and emits territorial calls at dawn.
curiosities: Vocalizations can be heard over great distances.
The tail helps in moving between branches.
bugio-preto.distribution: Central and eastern South America, including the Pantanal.
bugio-preto.ecologicalImportance: Disperses seeds and influences forest regeneration.

ariranha.description: Social and semi-aquatic mammal that hunts in rivers, bays and streams in the Pantanal.
ariranha.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, webbed paws, strong tail and light spots on the neck.
ariranha.habitat: Rivers, lagoons, bays and banks with plant shelter.
ariranha.behavior: It lives in family groups, vocalizes and hunts mainly fish.
ariranha.diet: Fish, crustaceans and small aquatic vertebrates.
curiosities: Each individual may have distinct light markings on the neck.
The species depends on relatively preserved and connected waters.
ariranha.distribution: River basins in South America, with an important population in the Pantanal.
ariranha.ecologicalImportance: It is a top predator in aquatic environments and indicates the quality of rivers.

lontra-neotropical.description: Otter with discreet habits that uses rivers, streams and lakes with vegetated banks.
lontra-neotropical.physicalCharacteristics: Fusiform body, partially webbed paws and dense brown fur.
lontra-neotropical.behavior: Loose or in small groups, it swims quickly and rests in holes and ravines.
lontra-neotropical.diet: Fish, crustaceans, amphibians and small vertebrates.
curiosities: It can leave marks and feces at crossing points on the banks.
Riparian vegetation offers shelter and resting places.
lontra-neotropical.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
lontra-neotropical.ecologicalImportance: It participates in the control of aquatic organisms and connects terrestrial and aquatic environments.

queixada.description: Social wild pig that forms groups and roams forested areas and mosaics of vegetation.
queixada.physicalCharacteristics: Dark coat, light stripe on the chin and compact body with strong legs.
queixada.habitat: Forests, riparian forests, wooded savannas and areas with availability of fruits and water.
queixada.behavior: It lives in groups, travels long distances and can use vocalizations and chemical signals to maintain social cohesion.
queixada.diet: Fruits, seeds, roots, leaves and small organisms found in the soil.
curiosities: Large groups can move across large areas.
The species uses vegetation and soil when searching for food.
queixada.distribution: From southern Mexico to northern Argentina, in different forest and savannah formations in South America.
queixada.ecologicalImportance: It acts on soil movement and seed dispersal or predation, connecting forest and forest floor processes.

mutum-de-penacho.description: Large forest bird that uses the soil and low vegetation to feed.
mutum-de-penacho.physicalCharacteristics: Predominantly dark male with white belly and females with more cryptic plumage, with evident plumage.
mutum-de-penacho.habitat: Woods, riverine forests and mosaics of vegetation in central South America.
mutum-de-penacho.behavior: It forages on the ground, moves in pairs or small groups and uses trees and dense vegetation for shelter.
mutum-de-penacho.diet: Fruits, seeds, leaves and small invertebrates found on the forest floor.
curiosities: Males and females have marked differences in plumage.
Forest loss and hunting pressure can affect local populations.
mutum-de-penacho.distribution: Central and southern Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay and adjacent regions of South America.
mutum-de-penacho.ecologicalImportance: It consumes and transports fruits and seeds, contributing to the dynamics of forests and riparian forests.

carau.description: Bird from humid areas, known for its loud call and search for snails among the vegetation.
carau.physicalCharacteristics: Striated brown plumage, long legs and curved beak.
carau.habitat: Swamps, flooded fields, bays and banks with macrophytes.
carau.behavior: It walks slowly in shallow waters and vocalizes at dawn and dusk.
carau.diet: Mainly snails and other aquatic invertebrates.
curiosities: The curved beak helps to remove mollusks from the shells.
It is often detected by song before sighting.
carau.distribution: Central and South America, including the entire Pantanal.
carau.ecologicalImportance: Regulates mollusk populations in flooded areas.

seriema.description: Long-legged land bird associated with open fields and formations in South America.
seriema.physicalCharacteristics: Brown plumage, reddish legs, strong beak and crest of feathers at the base of the beak.
seriema.habitat: Fields, savannas, savannas and edges of forest formations.
seriema.behavior: It walks and runs on the ground, vocalizes intensely and captures prey during terrestrial foraging.
seriema.diet: Insects, small vertebrates, eggs and other animals available in the environment.
curiosities: The vocalization can be heard over a long distance.
It is a predominantly terrestrial bird, although it can perch.
seriema.distribution: Open regions of central and eastern South America, including Brazil.
seriema.ecologicalImportance: It preys on invertebrates and small vertebrates and participates in grassland food chains.

teiú.description: Large lizard that occupies fields, edges and areas close to rural housing.
teiú.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, long tail, dark coloring with light spots and forked tongue.
teiú.habitat: Fields, forest edges, sandy soils and disturbed areas.
teiú.behavior: Active during the day, it explores the ground and shelters in burrows.
teiú.diet: Fruits, eggs, insects, small vertebrates and carrion.
curiosities: It is an opportunistic omnivore.
The tongue helps in collecting chemical information from the environment.
teiú.distribution: Eastern and central South America, including the Pantanal.
teiú.ecologicalImportance: Contributes to seed dispersal and control of small animals.

dourado.description: Predatory river fish, known for its golden color and importance in aquatic food chains.
dourado.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, golden scales, wide mouth and developed fins.
dourado.habitat: Rivers, streams and connected areas during the flood period.
dourado.behavior: An active swimmer, it travels through different stretches of rivers in search of prey.
dourado.diet: Fish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals.
curiosities: Flood dynamics influence access to feeding areas.
It is a species valued in river connectivity studies.
dourado.distribution: Paraná, Paraguay and other South American basins.
dourado.ecologicalImportance: Medium and large predator that regulates fish communities.

jaguatirica.description: Medium-sized feline, nocturnal and discreet, associated with forests and vegetation corridors.
jaguatirica.physicalCharacteristics: Yellowish coat with spots and rosettes, short tail and eyes adapted to low light.
jaguatirica.habitat: Riparian forests, capons, savannas and forest edges.
jaguatirica.diet: Small mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians.
curiosities: The spots help with camouflage between shadows and foliage.
You can use forest corridors to move between areas.
jaguatirica.distribution: Wide distribution in the Americas, including the Pantanal.

mao-pelada.description: Nocturnal mammal that explores riverbanks, humid areas and forests in search of food.
mao-pelada.physicalCharacteristics: Dark facial mask, ringed tail and long fingers.
mao-pelada.habitat: Riparian forests, wetlands, rivers and flooded areas.
mao-pelada.behavior: Nocturnal, solitary and skilled at manipulating food with its paws.
mao-pelada.diet: Crustaceans, fruits, insects, amphibians and small vertebrates.
curiosities: The sensitive paws help when searching for food in shallow water.
The ringed tail is a characteristic visual mark.
mao-pelada.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
mao-pelada.ecologicalImportance: Participates in the control of invertebrates and seed dispersal.

cachorro-do-mato.description: Generalist canid that occupies fields, savannas and forest edges in the Pantanal.
cachorro-do-mato.physicalCharacteristics: Brownish-gray coat, short legs and narrow snout.
cachorro-do-mato.habitat: Fields, savannas, open forests and altered areas.
cachorro-do-mato.behavior: Crepuscular and nocturnal activity, generally alone or in pairs.
cachorro-do-mato.diet: Fruits, insects, small vertebrates and carrion.
curiosities: Adapts to different environments and food resources.
It can act as a seed disperser of native fruits.
cachorro-do-mato.distribution: Much of South America, including the Pantanal.
cachorro-do-mato.ecologicalImportance: Connects food chains and disperses seeds.

macaco-prego.description: Intelligent arboreal primate, common in forest fragments and corridors of the Pantanal.
macaco-prego.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, dexterous hands, semi-prehensile tail and expressive face.
macaco-prego.habitat: Riparian forests, thickets and forest edges.
macaco-prego.behavior: Diurnal, social and active in the canopy and understory.
macaco-prego.diet: Fruits, seeds, leaves, insects and small animals.
curiosities: Uses hands to explore food and objects.
Lives in groups with complex social relationships.
macaco-prego.distribution: Central-southern South America, occurring in the Pantanal.

anhuma.description: Large water bird associated with humid areas, with a characteristic horny extension on the head.
anhuma.physicalCharacteristics: Dark body with light spots, strong legs and a thin horny structure projected on the forehead.
anhuma.habitat: Swamps, lake margins, flooded areas and aquatic vegetation.
anhuma.behavior: It feeds and moves close to water, being able to vocalize and fly between connected humid areas.
anhuma.diet: Leaves, shoots, aquatic plants and other plant items available on the banks.
curiosities: The popular name refers to the horny structure on the head.
The species usually remains close to humid environments with vegetation.
anhuma.distribution: Tropical South America, especially in basins and humid areas in the north and center of the continent.
anhuma.ecologicalImportance: Participates in the consumption and transport of plant matter in flooded environments.

urubu-rei.description: Large scavenging bird that uses forested and open areas in search of carcasses.
urubu-rei.physicalCharacteristics: Colorful head, white and black body, robust beak and wide wings.
urubu-rei.habitat: Woods, clearings, edges and open areas close to forests.
urubu-rei.behavior: It flies long distances and takes advantage of thermal currents to locate food.
curiosities: Its strong beak allows it to open resistant fabrics.
Carcass removal reduces organic matter available to pathogens.
urubu-rei.distribution: Central and South America, with records in the Pantanal.
urubu-rei.ecologicalImportance: It recycles nutrients and acts as an important environmental cleaning agent.

jacare-coroa.description: Small freshwater alligator associated with streams, rivers and forested areas.
jacare-coroa.physicalCharacteristics: Short snout, marked osteoderms and compact body.
jacare-coroa.habitat: Streams, creeks, smaller rivers and shaded banks.
jacare-coroa.behavior: Discreet, mainly nocturnal and dependent on shelters close to water.
jacare-coroa.diet: Fish, crustaceans, insects and small vertebrates.
curiosities: It is one of the smallest species of alligator.
The bony covering protects the back against impacts and predators.
jacare-coroa.distribution: South American basins, including areas of the Pantanal.
jacare-coroa.ecologicalImportance: It preys on aquatic organisms and helps balance stream chains.

traira.description: Predatory fish in calm waters, common in lagoons, streams and areas of aquatic vegetation.
traira.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, wide mouth and camouflaged brown color.
traira.habitat: Lagoons, bays, streams, slow rivers and flooded areas.
traira.behavior: Ambush predator, remains between submerged structures.
traira.diet: Fish, crustaceans, insects and small aquatic vertebrates.
curiosities: Camouflage favors quick attacks from cover.
Tolerates seasonal variations in oxygen in shallow waters.
traira.distribution: Wide distribution in South American basins, including the Pantanal.
traira.ecologicalImportance: Regulates populations of small fish and aquatic invertebrates.

cutia.description: Diurnal rodent that roams the understory and buries seeds in forested areas.
cutia.physicalCharacteristics: Compact body, long legs and brown fur.
cutia.habitat: Riparian forests, thickets and forest edges.
cutia.behavior: Diurnal, alert and generally solitary or in pairs.
curiosities: You can hide seeds for later consumption.
Their behavior helps transport seeds away from the mother plant.
cutia.distribution: South-central South America, including the Pantanal.
cutia.ecologicalImportance: It disperses and buries seeds, contributing to the regeneration of forests.

paca.description: Rodent with crepuscular and nocturnal habits, associated with forests close to water.
paca.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, light lateral spots and wide head.
paca.habitat: Riparian forests, capons and river banks.
paca.behavior: Discreet, it digs holes and looks for fruits in the ground.
paca.diet: Fruits, seeds and tender parts of plants.
curiosities: The proximity of water offers escape routes and shelter.
It is an important prey item for big cats and alligators.
paca.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
paca.ecologicalImportance: It disperses seeds and participates in the terrestrial food chain.

gato-mourisco.description: Feline with an elongated body that uses fields, savannas and forest edges.
gato-mourisco.physicalCharacteristics: Slender body, short legs, small head and variable uniform coat.
gato-mourisco.habitat: Fields, savannas, open forests and edges.
gato-mourisco.behavior: Solitary, active at different times and capable of occupying altered areas.
gato-mourisco.diet: Small mammals, birds, reptiles and invertebrates.
curiosities: The coat can vary between reddish, gray or dark tones.
Its elongated body makes it easier to move through dense vegetation.
gato-mourisco.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.

aracua.description: Social bird of edges and open forests, recognized by its noisy collective call.
aracua.physicalCharacteristics: Slender body, long tail and brown plumage with a light throat.
aracua.habitat: Riparian forests, thickets and forest edges.
aracua.behavior: It lives in groups and moves between trees and bushes in search of food.
curiosities: Groups may vocalize in chorus at dawn.
It is often seen on fruit trees.
aracua.distribution: Central South America, including the Pantanal.
aracua.ecologicalImportance: Disperses seeds of tree and shrub species.

soco-boi.description: Heron with discreet habits that hunts in shallow waters and vegetation banks.
soco-boi.physicalCharacteristics: Long neck, striated plumage and pointed beak.
soco-boi.habitat: Swamps, bays, streams and river banks.
soco-boi.behavior: It remains motionless waiting for prey and is most active at dusk.
soco-boi.diet: Fish, amphibians, crustaceans and aquatic insects.
curiosities: Immobility helps them approach aquatic prey.
Juvenile plumage is quite different from adult plumage.
soco-boi.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
soco-boi.ecologicalImportance: Controls organisms in flooded areas and integrates aquatic chains.

jacana.description: Bird from flooded areas that walks on floating leaves with very long fingers.
jacana.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated fingers and nails, dark body and yellow and red details.
jacana.habitat: Shallow lagoons, marshes and fields with floating aquatic plants.
jacana.behavior: It walks on vegetation and looks for invertebrates among leaves and water.
jacana.diet: Insects, small invertebrates, seeds and plant matter.
curiosities: Fingers distribute weight over floating leaves.
It can emit short calls when alarmed.
jacana.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
jacana.ecologicalImportance: Controls invertebrates and moves nutrients in shallow areas.

martim-pescador-grande.description: Riverine bird that observes the water from perches and dives to catch fish.
martim-pescador-grande.physicalCharacteristics: Large beak, robust body and evident crest.
martim-pescador-grande.habitat: Rivers, lagoons, bays and open banks.
martim-pescador-grande.behavior: Watch from branches and perform quick dives.
martim-pescador-grande.diet: Fish, crustaceans and small aquatic animals.
curiosities: The position of the perch helps calculate the dive.
It can be observed in open waters with good visibility.
martim-pescador-grande.ecologicalImportance: Integrates aquatic and terrestrial food chains.

curimbata.description: Migratory fish from South American rivers, important for the dynamics of floods and aquatic chains.
curimbata.physicalCharacteristics: Fusiform body, mouth adapted to scraping and silvery scales.
curimbata.habitat: Rivers, canals, streams and areas flooded during floods.
curimbata.behavior: It forms schools and makes seasonal movements for reproduction and feeding.
curimbata.diet: Debris, algae and organic matter from the bottom.
curiosities: Migration depends on river connectivity.
Bottom feeding moves sediment and nutrients.
curimbata.ecologicalImportance: Transports energy and nutrients between rivers and floodplains.

cagado-de-barbicha.description: Freshwater turtle that occupies rivers, lakes and banks with available shelters.
cagado-de-barbicha.physicalCharacteristics: Oval carapace, broad head and wattles under the chin.
cagado-de-barbicha.habitat: Rivers, streams, lagoons and banks of slow waters.
cagado-de-barbicha.behavior: Aquatic, opportunistic and often observed sunning on logs.
cagado-de-barbicha.diet: Small fish, invertebrates, carcasses and plant matter.
curiosities: Barbels help with perception of the aquatic environment.
The quality of the banks influences their shelter locations.
cagado-de-barbicha.distribution: Basins of central and eastern South America, including the Pantanal.
cagado-de-barbicha.ecologicalImportance: Participates in the control of aquatic organisms and recycling of matter.

cobra-verde.description: Green arboreal snake, found in forests, bushes and vegetated edges.
cobra-verde.physicalCharacteristics: Slender body, green scales and long tail.
cobra-verde.habitat: Forests, thickets, bushes and edges with dense vegetation.
cobra-verde.diet: Small vertebrates, amphibians, lizards and birds.
curiosities: The coloring offers camouflage between leaves.
Like all snakes, it must be observed without attempting to capture it.
cobra-verde.ecologicalImportance: It controls small vertebrates and integrates the forest food chain.

perereca-cabecuda.description: Amphibian of humid areas and vegetated edges, active mainly at night.
perereca-cabecuda.physicalCharacteristics: Slender body, large eyes, adhesive discs on the fingers and variable coloring.
perereca-cabecuda.habitat: Swamps, temporary lagoons, flooded areas and vegetation close to water.
perereca-cabecuda.behavior: Nocturnal, it vocalizes during the rainy season and rests in vegetation.
curiosities: The song helps locate individuals during the rainy season.
Sensitive skin makes the species vulnerable to water pollution.
perereca-cabecuda.distribution: Central and eastern South America, including the Pantanal.
perereca-cabecuda.ecologicalImportance: Controls insects and works as an indicator of environmental quality.

ra-quatro-olhos.description: Small land frog that takes advantage of temporary puddles formed by rain.
ra-quatro-olhos.physicalCharacteristics: Compact body, dorsal spots and glands that resemble eyes in the posterior region.
ra-quatro-olhos.habitat: Fields, sandy soils and temporary puddles.
ra-quatro-olhos.behavior: Nocturnal and explosive after heavy rain, when it reproduces quickly.
curiosities: Temporary puddles are essential for their reproductive cycle.
The posterior markings can confuse predators.
ra-quatro-olhos.distribution: Open regions of South America, with records in central Brazil.
ra-quatro-olhos.ecologicalImportance: It controls invertebrates and serves as food for birds, reptiles and mammals.

piranha-vermelha.description: Fish with sharp teeth that occupies slow waters, bays, streams and lagoons in the Pantanal.
piranha-vermelha.physicalCharacteristics: Tall body, silvery color with reddish belly and strong teeth.
piranha-vermelha.habitat: Slow rivers, bays, streams and floodplain lagoons.
piranha-vermelha.behavior: It forms schools and responds to opportunities for food and shelter.
piranha-vermelha.diet: Fish, invertebrates, fruits and animal matter.
curiosities: The species participates in complex food webs and is not defined solely by aggressive behavior.
Flood dynamics influence their local distribution.
piranha-vermelha.distribution: Basins of northern and central South America, including the Pantanal.
piranha-vermelha.ecologicalImportance: Regulates fish populations and recycles organic matter.

tuvira.description: Electric fish of calm waters, active among roots, plants and submerged structures.
tuvira.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, absence of dorsal fin and undulating anal region.
tuvira.habitat: Corixos, lagoons, bays and banks with aquatic vegetation.
tuvira.behavior: Nocturnal, uses weak electrical signals for orientation and communication.
curiosities: Electrical signals aid navigation in murky water.
The dynamics of floods expand their available habitat.
tuvira.distribution: Paraguay Basin and associated regions of central South America.
tuvira.ecologicalImportance: It integrates food chains and controls small aquatic organisms.

morfoborboleta.description: Butterfly with blue wings that frequents clearings, edges and forest trails.
morfoborboleta.physicalCharacteristics: Wide wings with metallic blue shine on males and ocelli patterns on the back.
morfoborboleta.habitat: Riparian forests, thickets, clearings and forest edges.
morfoborboleta.behavior: It flies in broad trajectories and visits sunny areas for thermoregulation.
morfoborboleta.diet: Adults consume fruit liquids and organic matter; caterpillars use host plants.
curiosities: The blue glow results from the structure of the scales, not from simple pigment.
The back of the wings is more discreet and favors camouflage.
morfoborboleta.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
morfoborboleta.ecologicalImportance: Participates in pollination and forest food chains.

besouro-rola-bosta.description: Scarabee beetle that uses organic matter and contributes to nutrient cycling.
besouro-rola-bosta.physicalCharacteristics: Compact body, legs adapted to digging and strong jaws.
besouro-rola-bosta.habitat: Fields, open forests and soils with organic matter availability.
besouro-rola-bosta.behavior: Locates resources by scent, forms and transports small balls of material.
curiosities: Burying the resource improves the incorporation of nutrients into the soil.
Activity varies with humidity and temperature.
besouro-rola-bosta.distribution: South America, with records in Brazilian environments.
besouro-rola-bosta.ecologicalImportance: Recycles nutrients, aerating the soil and dispersing seeds present in organic material.

biguá.description: Water bird that dives to capture fish in rivers, bays and streams.
biguá.physicalCharacteristics: Dark plumage, long neck and beak with a curved tip.
biguá.habitat: Rivers, lagoons, bays, streams and open banks.
biguá.behavior: It dives and swims efficiently, drying its wings after fishing.
biguá.diet: Fish, crustaceans and small aquatic animals.
curiosities: The plumage can be exposed to the sun after diving.
It is a visual indicator of the presence of fish in open waters.
biguá.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
biguá.ecologicalImportance: It participates in fish control and the transfer of nutrients between water and land.

garca-moura.description: Large heron that hunts motionless on banks, flooded fields and shallow waters.
garca-moura.physicalCharacteristics: Long neck, long legs, gray back and light chest.
garca-moura.habitat: Rivers, bays, swamps, streams and flooded fields.
garca-moura.behavior: Walks slowly or remains motionless waiting for prey.
garca-moura.diet: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, crustaceans and small mammals.
curiosities: The immobile posture reduces prey alertness.
You can use tall trees for resting and nesting.
garca-moura.distribution: South America, including the entire Pantanal.
garca-moura.ecologicalImportance: Integrates aquatic and terrestrial food chains.

soco-dorminhoco.description: Heron with crepuscular and nocturnal habits that uses banks and aquatic vegetation.
soco-dorminhoco.physicalCharacteristics: Compact body, red eyes in adults and robust beak.
soco-dorminhoco.habitat: Swamps, lagoons, rivers, canals and flooded areas with shelter.
soco-dorminhoco.behavior: It rests during the day and goes hunting at dusk and at night.
soco-dorminhoco.diet: Fish, amphibians, insects, crustaceans and small vertebrates.
curiosities: Young people have brown striated plumage that is very different from that of adults.
It can form breeding colonies in trees near water.
soco-dorminhoco.distribution: Americas and other regions, with widespread occurrence in the Pantanal.
soco-dorminhoco.ecologicalImportance: Controls aquatic and terrestrial organisms in humid areas.

coruja-buraqueira.description: A land owl that occupies open fields and uses burrows for shelter and reproduction.
coruja-buraqueira.physicalCharacteristics: Small body, yellow eyes, long legs and upright posture.
coruja-buraqueira.habitat: Fields, pastures, open areas and rural roadsides.
coruja-buraqueira.behavior: It is active day and night, observing its surroundings from the ground or low perches.
coruja-buraqueira.diet: Insects, small rodents, lizards and amphibians.
curiosities: It can occupy burrows abandoned by mammals.
Moves head and body quickly when investigating threats.
coruja-buraqueira.ecologicalImportance: Controls insects and small vertebrates in open areas.

lambari-do-pantanal.description: Small schooling fish present in calm, flowing waters of the floodplain.
lambari-do-pantanal.physicalCharacteristics: Silver body, small scales and delicate fins.
lambari-do-pantanal.habitat: Rivers, streams, lagoons and flooded fields.
lambari-do-pantanal.behavior: It forms schools and looks for food among plants and banks.
lambari-do-pantanal.diet: Insects, algae, fruits and small invertebrates.
curiosities: Schools respond quickly to shadows and movement on the bank.
Small fish are important to larger predators.
lambari-do-pantanal.distribution: Basins in central and southern Brazil, including the Paraguay system.
lambari-do-pantanal.ecologicalImportance: Transfers energy from small resources to predatory fish, birds and reptiles.

mandi.description: Bottom catfish that looks for food among rocks, logs and river sediments.
mandi.physicalCharacteristics: Long barbels, spots on the body and fins with spines.
mandi.habitat: Rivers, canals, streams and stretches with varied background.
mandi.behavior: Most active at dusk and at night, exploring the bottom.
mandi.diet: Invertebrates, small fish and organic matter.
curiosities: Barbels help find food in murky water.
The connectivity of rivers favors their movement.
mandi.distribution: Paraná, Paraguay and other South American basins.
mandi.ecologicalImportance: It recycles organic matter and participates in the aquatic food chain.

pitu.description: Freshwater shrimp that occupy rivers, lakes and flooded areas with plant shelter.
pitu.physicalCharacteristics: Segmented body, long antennae and developed chelae.
pitu.habitat: Rivers, streams, lagoons, submerged roots and vegetated banks.
pitu.behavior: Explore the bottom and vegetation, especially at night.
pitu.diet: Debris, algae, small animals and organic matter.
curiosities: The shape of its body allows it to hide in submerged roots and leaves.
Floods expand the places available for feeding and dispersal.
pitu.distribution: South American basins, with records in Brazilian freshwater environments.
pitu.ecologicalImportance: It recycles organic matter and serves as food for fish and birds.

libelula-pantaneira.description: Migratory dragonfly observed over open areas and temporary bodies of water.
libelula-pantaneira.physicalCharacteristics: Long wings, narrow abdomen and yellowish to brown coloration.
libelula-pantaneira.habitat: Temporary ponds, marshes, fields and open areas close to water.
libelula-pantaneira.behavior: It flies long distances and hunts insects during the day.
libelula-pantaneira.diet: Mosquitoes, flies and other flying insects.
curiosities: The species is known for long-distance movement.
Nymphs live in water before metamorphosis.
libelula-pantaneira.distribution: Widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions, including the Pantanal.
libelula-pantaneira.ecologicalImportance: Controls flying insects and connects aquatic and terrestrial environments.

tamandua-mirim.description: Medium-sized anteater that explores the ground and trees in search of ants and termites.
tamandua-mirim.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated snout, strong claws, prehensile tail and variable dark stripe.
tamandua-mirim.habitat: Riparian forests, thickets, savannas and fields with shelter.
tamandua-mirim.behavior: Solitary, active day or night and able to climb trees.
tamandua-mirim.diet: Ants, termites and other small invertebrates.
curiosities: The long tongue reaches insect colonies in cracks.
The claws are also used for defense and digging.
tamandua-mirim.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.

irara.description: Agile mustelid that runs through trees and soil in forests and edges of the Pantanal.
irara.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, strong legs, long tail and light or dark head.
irara.habitat: Riparian forests, capons, wooded savannas and edges.
irara.behavior: Diurnal, curious, solitary or observed in small family groups.
irara.diet: Fruits, small vertebrates, insects and honey.
curiosities: Moves easily between soil and trees.
Its popular name also appears in records from other Brazilian regions.
irara.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
irara.ecologicalImportance: It preys on small animals and disperses seeds.

quati.description: Mammal with a mobile snout that searches for fruits and small animals on the ground and in trees.
quati.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated snout, ringed tail and claws adapted for digging.
quati.habitat: Forests, thickets, edges and areas close to watercourses.
quati.behavior: Females and young live in groups; Adult males are often solitary.
quati.diet: Fruits, insects, eggs, small vertebrates and organic matter.
curiosities: The flexible snout helps it explore leaves and trunks.
The raised tail helps the group's visual communication.

carrapateiro.description: Generalist bird of prey, common in open areas and forest edges.
carrapateiro.physicalCharacteristics: Light head, dark back and wide wings.
carrapateiro.habitat: Fields, pastures, edges and areas close to livestock farming.
carrapateiro.behavior: It lands in high places and looks for food on the ground or on other animals.
carrapateiro.diet: Ticks, insects, carrion, small vertebrates and food remains.
curiosities: It can remove ectoparasites from large mammals.
Take advantage of modified environments without abandoning natural areas.
carrapateiro.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
carrapateiro.ecologicalImportance: Controls invertebrates and removes organic matter.

gaviao-caramujeiro.description: Bird of prey specialized in searching for snails and other resources in humid areas.
gaviao-caramujeiro.physicalCharacteristics: Curved beak, wide wings and claws adapted for capture.
gaviao-caramujeiro.habitat: Swamps, bays, flooded fields and banks with macrophytes.
gaviao-caramujeiro.behavior: It flies over humid areas and lands on vegetation close to the water.
curiosities: The curved beak is suitable for removing mollusks from their shells.
The presence follows the availability of flooded areas.
gaviao-caramujeiro.distribution: Central and South America, including the Pantanal.
gaviao-caramujeiro.ecologicalImportance: Regulates mollusc populations in flooded environments.

pica-pau-do-campo.description: Ground woodpecker that searches for insects on logs, soil and open areas.
pica-pau-do-campo.physicalCharacteristics: Contrasting plumage, strong beak and stiff tail for support.
pica-pau-do-campo.habitat: Fields, savannas, pastures and edges with sparse trees.
pica-pau-do-campo.behavior: It alternates between the ground and perches, using its beak to explore wood and earth.
pica-pau-do-campo.diet: Ants, termites, larvae and other invertebrates.
curiosities: It may forage more on the ground than many other woodpeckers.
The rigid tail helps with climbing trunks.
pica-pau-do-campo.ecologicalImportance: Controls insects and creates cavities that can be used by other species.

tesourinha.description: Insectivorous passerine with a forked tail, seen in fields and open areas.
tesourinha.physicalCharacteristics: Long, deeply forked tail, dark back and light belly.
tesourinha.habitat: Fields, pastures, savannas and forest edges.
tesourinha.behavior: It makes rapid flights from perches to capture insects.
curiosities: The tail can vary in size depending on age and sex.
It carries out seasonal movements in a large part of the distribution.

sucuri-amarela.description: Large semiaquatic snake associated with rivers, bays and seasonally flooded areas.
sucuri-amarela.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, dark spots and yellowish or olive color.
sucuri-amarela.habitat: Swamps, banks, bays and slow-flowing watercourses.
sucuri-amarela.behavior: It swims well, hunts by ambush and uses water for thermoregulation.
sucuri-amarela.diet: Fish, birds, mammals and other vertebrates.
curiosities: It has no venom and subdues prey by constriction.
Floods increase connectivity between their environments.
sucuri-amarela.distribution: Paraguay Basin and other areas of South America, including the Pantanal.
sucuri-amarela.ecologicalImportance: Top predator in aquatic and riparian environments.

teiu.description: Large terrestrial lizard that uses open areas, edges and forested environments.
teiu.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, long tail, dark coloring with light spots and strong limbs.
teiu.habitat: Fields, savannas, forest edges and clearings with shelter and food supply.
teiu.behavior: It forages mainly on the ground, alternating periods of activity with shelter in holes and cavities.
teiu.diet: Fruits, eggs, insects, small vertebrates and other items found while foraging.
curiosities: The long tail helps with balance and locomotion.
May use burrows and ground shelters for protection.
teiu.distribution: Regions of eastern and central South America, including much of Brazil.
teiu.ecologicalImportance: Participates in the control of invertebrates and the movement of seeds and organic matter in the soil.

perereca-de-cera.description: Arboreal tree frog adapted to hot and seasonally dry environments in the Pantanal.
perereca-de-cera.physicalCharacteristics: Green body, vertical pupils and skin with waxy secretions.
perereca-de-cera.habitat: Shrub vegetation, open forests and areas close to temporary bodies of water.
perereca-de-cera.behavior: Nocturnal, arboreal and active mainly after rain.
curiosities: The waxy secretion helps reduce water loss.
It lays eggs on leaves that are above the water.
perereca-de-cera.distribution: Central South America, including areas of the Pantanal.
perereca-de-cera.ecologicalImportance: Controls insects and indicates the availability of moist microhabitats.

ra-pimenta-pantanal.description: Large frog that breeds in temporary pools and damp banks.
ra-pimenta-pantanal.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, spotted back and muscular hind limbs.
ra-pimenta-pantanal.habitat: Puddles, swamps, floodable fields and forest edges.
ra-pimenta-pantanal.behavior: Nocturnal, it vocalizes after rain and can defend its shelter.
curiosities: Builds foam nests to protect reproduction.
It is one of the largest frogs found in open Brazilian environments.
ra-pimenta-pantanal.distribution: Central and southern Brazil, including the Pantanal.
ra-pimenta-pantanal.ecologicalImportance: Controls invertebrates and integrates the food chain in wetlands.

traira-pantanal.description: Predatory fish in slow waters, resistant to seasonal variations and low oxygenation.
traira-pantanal.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, wide mouth, strong teeth and cryptic coloring.
traira-pantanal.habitat: Bays, streams, lagoons, marshes and vegetated banks.
traira-pantanal.behavior: It lurks among plants and attacks prey with quick movements.
traira-pantanal.diet: Fish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals.
curiosities: It can survive in environments with little oxygen.
The coloring helps in ambushing between submerged leaves and branches.
traira-pantanal.distribution: South America, including the Pantanal basins.
traira-pantanal.ecologicalImportance: Regulates populations of small fish and connects different trophic levels.

piau-tres-pintas.description: Fish with scales marked by dark spots, common in rivers and environments connected by floods.
piau-tres-pintas.physicalCharacteristics: Fusiform body, developed fins and three characteristic lateral spots.
piau-tres-pintas.habitat: Rivers, streams, bays and connected wetlands.
piau-tres-pintas.behavior: It forms schools and looks for food near the bottom and vegetation.
piau-tres-pintas.diet: Fruits, seeds, algae and small invertebrates.
curiosities: Migration between rivers and flooded areas follows the flood pulse.
Fallen fruit can be important during flooding.
piau-tres-pintas.distribution: South American basins, including the Pantanal.
piau-tres-pintas.ecologicalImportance: Participates in seed dispersal and aquatic energy flow.

caranguejo-de-agua-doce.description: Freshwater crab found on banks, aquatic vegetation and bottoms of swamp environments.
caranguejo-de-agua-doce.physicalCharacteristics: Flattened carapace, developed chelae and legs adapted to fresh water.
caranguejo-de-agua-doce.habitat: Rivers, bays, streams and flooded areas with plant shelter.
caranguejo-de-agua-doce.behavior: Explore the bottom and banks, especially at dusk and at night.
caranguejo-de-agua-doce.diet: Debris, algae, plants and small invertebrates.
curiosities: Molting is a period of greater vulnerability.
You can take advantage of shelters between submerged roots and leaves.
caranguejo-de-agua-doce.distribution: Paraguay Basin and other freshwater areas of South America.
caranguejo-de-agua-doce.ecologicalImportance: It recycles organic matter and serves as food for fish and birds.

lobo-guara.description: Long-legged canid associated with open environments and savannah formations in South America.
lobo-guara.physicalCharacteristics: Predominantly orange coat, dark legs, dorsal mane and large ears.
lobo-guara.habitat: Fields, savannas, savannas and open areas with interspersed vegetation cover.
lobo-guara.behavior: Generally solitary and crepuscular or nocturnal, moving across large areas in search of food.
lobo-guara.diet: Fruits, small vertebrates and invertebrates, with an important participation of the lobeira fruit in their diet.
curiosities: The species is the largest canid in South America.
Their communication includes scent marking and vocalizations.
lobo-guara.distribution: Central South America, mainly in cerrado areas and open formations in Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Peru and Argentina.
lobo-guara.ecologicalImportance: It acts as a predator of small animals and a seed disperser in open environments.

cateto.description: Small wild pig with wide distribution, found in forested and open environments with shelter.
cateto.physicalCharacteristics: Gray or brown coat, light stripe similar to a collar on the neck and robust body.
cateto.habitat: Forests, savannas, forest edges and areas with shelter and access to water.
cateto.behavior: It lives in small groups or family groups, uses vocalizations and scent markings and explores the soil in search of food.
cateto.diet: Fruits, seeds, roots, leaves, cacti and small invertebrates.
curiosities: The light stripe on the neck helps distinguish the peccary from other wild pigs.
Scent glands participate in communication between individuals.
cateto.distribution: From the southwestern United States to South America, including much of Brazil.
cateto.ecologicalImportance: It turns the soil, influences the availability of seeds and participates in food chains as a consumer and prey.

cobra-cipo.description: Slender, arboreal snake that moves between branches and foliage in tropical environments.
cobra-cipo.physicalCharacteristics: Very slender body, elongated head and coloring that favors camouflage among branches and leaves.
cobra-cipo.habitat: Forests, forest edges and shrub vegetation with structures for arboreal locomotion.
cobra-cipo.behavior: It remains among the vegetation, observing its surroundings and capturing prey by approaching and quickly lunging.
cobra-cipo.diet: Small vertebrates, especially lizards and other animals of compatible size.
curiosities: The thin body produces a twig-like silhouette.
The elongated head is a striking characteristic of the genus.
cobra-cipo.distribution: Wide distribution in the tropical Americas, occurring in different forest and savanna environments.
cobra-cipo.ecologicalImportance: It integrates arboreal food chains as a predator of small vertebrates.

perereca-do-banheiro.description: Tree frog with arboreal habits associated with humid environments and vegetation close to bodies of water.
perereca-do-banheiro.physicalCharacteristics: Compact body, adhesive discs on the fingers and variable coloring in yellowish and brownish tones.
perereca-do-banheiro.habitat: Swamps, lake margins, riparian vegetation and humid areas with vertical shelter.
perereca-do-banheiro.behavior: It vocalizes mainly during reproductive periods and uses vegetation for rest and movement.
perereca-do-banheiro.diet: Small arthropods captured during night foraging.
curiosities: The adhesive discs help to climb leaves and branches.
Reproduction depends on the availability of water and moist microenvironments.
perereca-do-banheiro.distribution: South America, with records in different areas of Brazil and neighboring countries.
perereca-do-banheiro.ecologicalImportance: It participates in the control of small invertebrates and integrates the food chains of humid areas.

perereca-macaco.description: Arboreal tree frog with nocturnal habits that occupies branches and leaves in seasonal tropical environments.
perereca-macaco.physicalCharacteristics: Green body, big eyes, fingers with adhesive discs and adaptations for life on vegetation.
perereca-macaco.habitat: Forests, wooded savannas and borders with shrubs and trees suitable for arboreal life.
perereca-macaco.behavior: It remains on the vegetation and reproduces in leaves folded over the water, where the tadpoles complete their development.
perereca-macaco.diet: Arthropods and other small invertebrates captured in vegetation.
curiosities: Laying on folded leaves reduces direct exposure of eggs.
Waxy skin helps reduce water loss in seasonal environments.
perereca-macaco.distribution: Dry, seasonal regions of central South America, including areas of Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay and Argentina.
perereca-macaco.ecologicalImportance: Controls small invertebrates and transfers energy between vegetation and nocturnal predators.

gaviao-belo.description: Bird of prey associated with rivers, bays and flooded areas, specialized in capturing aquatic prey.
gaviao-belo.physicalCharacteristics: Brown plumage, light head, wide wings and strong claws.
gaviao-belo.habitat: Banks of rivers, lagoons, bays and aquatic vegetation.
gaviao-belo.behavior: It lands near the water and dives or descends quickly to capture prey.
gaviao-belo.diet: Fish and other small aquatic animals.
curiosities: Vision helps locate prey in shallow waters.
Landing on branches over water favors ambush hunting.
gaviao-belo.ecologicalImportance: Participates in fish control and food dynamics in wetlands.

cachara.description: Large catfish with a reticulated pattern, important in the rivers and bays of the Pantanal.
cachara.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, sensory wattles, flattened head and web-like spots.
cachara.habitat: River channels, bays, streams and deep connected areas.
cachara.behavior: Mainly nocturnal predator, using its barbels to locate prey.
curiosities: The barbels help with orientation in murky waters.
River connectivity is important for the life cycle.
cachara.distribution: Paraguay Basin and other South American basins.
cachara.ecologicalImportance: Top predator in freshwater environments and indicator of river connectivity.

veado-campeiro.description: Open range deer that uses seasonally flooded fields and vegetation edges.
veado-campeiro.physicalCharacteristics: Slender body, light brown fur and antlers in adult males.
veado-campeiro.habitat: Fields, savannas, savannas and open areas of the Pantanal.
veado-campeiro.behavior: It moves in small groups and alternates between feeding, watching and resting.
veado-campeiro.diet: Grasses, leaves, shoots and other plants available.
curiosities: Antlers are renewed periodically in males.
The openness of the landscape favors the detection of predators.
veado-campeiro.distribution: Central and eastern South America, including areas of the Pantanal.
veado-campeiro.ecologicalImportance: It participates in herbivory and transports seeds between open environments.

morcego-pescador.description: Bat associated with aquatic environments, capable of locating prey on the surface of the water.
morcego-pescador.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, large feet and claws adapted to capture aquatic prey.
morcego-pescador.habitat: Banks of rivers, lagoons, bays and wetlands.
morcego-pescador.behavior: Active at night, it flies close to the water and uses echolocation to forage.
morcego-pescador.diet: Small fish, crustaceans and aquatic insects.
curiosities: Sensory structures help detect ripples in the water.
Shelters can occur in hollows, foliage and structures close to rivers.
morcego-pescador.distribution: Tropical America, with records in Brazilian basins.
morcego-pescador.ecologicalImportance: Controls invertebrates and small fish, connecting aquatic and terrestrial chains.

ourico-cacheiro.description: Arboreal rodent with nocturnal habits that explores forest canopies and edges.
ourico-cacheiro.physicalCharacteristics: Body covered in spines, prehensile tail and paws adapted for climbing.
ourico-cacheiro.habitat: Riparian forests, forests and edges with trees and vines.
ourico-cacheiro.behavior: It moves slowly through the trees and remains hidden during the day.
ourico-cacheiro.diet: Leaves, fruits, bark, shoots and seeds.
curiosities: The tail helps with support while climbing.
The spines function as a defense against predators.
ourico-cacheiro.distribution: Tropical South America, including the Pantanal.
ourico-cacheiro.ecologicalImportance: Participates in herbivory and movement of seeds in vegetation.

arara-caninde.description: Large macaw with blue and yellow plumage, associated with forests and open areas with tall trees.
arara-caninde.physicalCharacteristics: Blue wings, yellow breast, strong beak and long tail.
arara-caninde.habitat: Riparian forests, open forests, edges and palm groves.
arara-caninde.behavior: It lives in pairs or groups and uses hollow trees for rest and reproduction.
arara-caninde.diet: Fruits, seeds, nuts and parts of plants.
curiosities: The beak breaks tough seeds.
Group travel can connect different forest fragments.
arara-caninde.distribution: Tropical South America, including areas of the Pantanal.
arara-caninde.ecologicalImportance: It disperses seeds and depends on mature trees for shelter and nesting.

urubu-de-cabeca-preta.description: Scavenger bird common in open areas, cities, riverbanks and forest edges.
urubu-de-cabeca-preta.physicalCharacteristics: Dark plumage, head without feathers, wide wings and gliding flight.
urubu-de-cabeca-preta.habitat: Fields, edges, urbanized areas and margins of aquatic environments.
urubu-de-cabeca-preta.behavior: It forms groups, uses thermal currents and locates carcasses by vision and collective behavior.
urubu-de-cabeca-preta.diet: Carcasses, organic remains and small dead animals.
curiosities: Gliding reduces energy expenditure.
Carcass removal contributes to nutrient cycling.
urubu-de-cabeca-preta.distribution: Americas, with wide occurrence in Brazil and the Pantanal.
urubu-de-cabeca-preta.ecologicalImportance: Recycles organic matter and helps reduce exposed decomposition sources.

tucano-toco.description: Toucan with a large beak that explores fruit trees, savannas and forest edges.
tucano-toco.physicalCharacteristics: Large orange beak, black plumage and white throat.
tucano-toco.habitat: Open forests, savannas, edges and forest thickets.
tucano-toco.behavior: It moves between trees and swallows whole fruits, forming pairs or small groups.
tucano-toco.diet: Fruits, eggs, chicks of other birds and small vertebrates.
curiosities: The beak participates in thermoregulation and obtaining food.
The species can use natural hollows for nesting.
tucano-toco.distribution: Central and eastern South America, including the Pantanal.
tucano-toco.ecologicalImportance: Disperses seeds and influences the regeneration of plant species.

cangapara.description: Freshwater chelon associated with flooded areas, vegetated banks and slow-moving environments.
cangapara.physicalCharacteristics: Dark and robust carapace, broad head and limbs adapted to freshwater.
cangapara.habitat: Bays, streams, lagoons and banks with aquatic vegetation.
cangapara.behavior: Alternate periods in the water and in resting places on the banks.
cangapara.diet: Invertebrates, small animals, plants and organic matter.
curiosities: The carapace offers protection from predators.
The quality of the banks influences shelter and food.
cangapara.distribution: Paraguay Basin and humid areas of central South America.
cangapara.ecologicalImportance: It participates in the flow of matter between bottoms, banks and shallow waters.

cobra-dagua.description: Aquatic snake that uses bodies of water and vegetated banks to hunt and shelter.
cobra-dagua.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, smooth scales and pattern that helps with camouflage among vegetation.
cobra-dagua.habitat: Lagoons, corixos, marshes and river banks.
cobra-dagua.behavior: It swims easily and looks for prey in shallow waters and among plants.
cobra-dagua.diet: Fish, tadpoles and small aquatic animals.
curiosities: The hydrodynamic body makes swimming easier.
Coloring can break the contour between shadows and vegetation.
cobra-dagua.distribution: Humid regions of southern and central South America.
cobra-dagua.ecologicalImportance: Controls small aquatic vertebrates and integrates the food chain in wetlands.

jacare-pagua.description: Alligator abundant in rivers, bays and streams, adapted to the annual cycle of floods and droughts.
jacare-pagua.physicalCharacteristics: Elongated body, wide snout, dermal plates and muscular tail.
jacare-pagua.habitat: Rivers, lagoons, bays, streams and floodable fields.
jacare-pagua.behavior: It basks on the banks, hunts in the water and can form concentrations during seasonal periods.
jacare-pagua.diet: Fish, crustaceans, insects and small vertebrates.
curiosities: Temperature influences activity and reproduction.
Low water areas concentrate food during drought.
jacare-pagua.distribution: Paraguay Basin and other humid areas of central South America.
jacare-pagua.ecologicalImportance: Aquatic predator and indicator of the integrity of humid environments.

tei-de-cauda-vermelha.description: Large terrestrial lizard that explores open areas, edges and shelters in the ground.
tei-de-cauda-vermelha.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, long tail, strong claws and reddish color.
tei-de-cauda-vermelha.habitat: Fields, savannas, forest edges and areas with soil for excavation.
tei-de-cauda-vermelha.behavior: Diurnal, opportunistic and capable of using burrows for shelter and thermoregulation.
tei-de-cauda-vermelha.diet: Fruits, eggs, insects, small vertebrates and carrion.
curiosities: The broad diet allows them to explore seasonal environments.
Excavation creates refuges used in times of heat or threat.
tei-de-cauda-vermelha.distribution: Central-southern South America, occurring in open formations.
tei-de-cauda-vermelha.ecologicalImportance: It preys, removes organic matter and can disperse seeds.

sapinho-cururu.description: Large frog that occupies open areas and edges, especially close to damp shelters.
sapinho-cururu.physicalCharacteristics: Rough skin, developed parotoid glands and robust body.
sapinho-cururu.habitat: Fields, gardens, forest edges and edges of wetlands.
sapinho-cururu.behavior: Active mainly at night and after rain, when looking for food and mates.
sapinho-cururu.diet: Insects, spiders and other small invertebrates.
curiosities: Rough skin helps with camouflage and protection.
Reproduction usually follows the onset of rain.
sapinho-cururu.distribution: South America, with wide occurrence in Brazilian areas.
sapinho-cururu.ecologicalImportance: It controls invertebrates and serves as food for specialized predators.

rã-pimenta.description: Terrestrial frog of open and humid areas, associated with temporary pools and vegetated banks.
rã-pimenta.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, brown coloring and strong hind limbs.
rã-pimenta.habitat: Floodable fields, marshes, temporary puddles and lake banks.
rã-pimenta.behavior: It remains hidden during dry periods and vocalizes after rain.
rã-pimenta.diet: Insects, larvae, spiders and small invertebrates.
curiosities: Temporary puddles can be important for reproduction.
Activity increases with favorable humidity and temperature.
rã-pimenta.distribution: Paraguay Basin and other humid regions of central South America.
rã-pimenta.ecologicalImportance: Controls invertebrates and indicates the availability of moist microhabitats.

perereca-fuscomarginata.description: Small tree frog that uses low vegetation and humid areas close to bodies of water.
perereca-fuscomarginata.physicalCharacteristics: Small body, adhesive discs on the fingers and dark side stripe.
perereca-fuscomarginata.habitat: Grass, shrubs, edges and vegetation around puddles.
perereca-fuscomarginata.behavior: Vocalizes over leaves and branches during the rainy season.
curiosities: The adhesive discs allow you to climb onto smooth sheets.
Vocalization helps locate individuals amid vegetation.
perereca-fuscomarginata.distribution: Central Brazil and other areas of tropical South America.
perereca-fuscomarginata.ecologicalImportance: Controls small arthropods and integrates the fauna of temporary pools.

perereca-folhagem-azul.description: Arboreal tree frog with nocturnal habits that uses leaves and branches in forest environments.
perereca-folhagem-azul.physicalCharacteristics: Green body, long limbs, adhesive discs and contrasting color on the internal parts.
perereca-folhagem-azul.habitat: Riparian forests, bushes, thickets and edges close to water.
perereca-folhagem-azul.behavior: It moves slowly through vegetation and remains motionless during the day.
curiosities: Standing still reduces the chance of being detected.
Reproduction depends on leaves and water in close environments.
perereca-folhagem-azul.distribution: Central South America, including the Chaco and Pantanal regions.
perereca-folhagem-azul.ecologicalImportance: It participates in insect control and indicates the quality of riparian vegetation.

jau.description: Large freshwater catfish that occupies deep stretches of rivers and environments connected by floods.
jau.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, broad head, sensory wattles and strong caudal fin.
jau.habitat: Deep gutters, river pits, streams and connected bays.
jau.behavior: Bottom predator, more active in periods of lower light.
jau.diet: Fish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals.
curiosities: The barbels help with orientation in murky waters.
River connectivity is important for movement and reproduction.
jau.distribution: Paraguay Basin and other basins in central South America.
jau.ecologicalImportance: Large predator and indicator of the integrity of deep rivers.

peixe-cachorro.description: Predatory fish with an elongated body that hunts in open waters and riverbanks.
peixe-cachorro.physicalCharacteristics: Silvery body, caniniform teeth and caudal fin adapted to fast swimming.
peixe-cachorro.habitat: Rivers, streams, lagoons and backwater areas.
peixe-cachorro.behavior: It forms small groups and quickly attacks smaller prey.
curiosities: The dentition is a striking characteristic of the group.
Marginal vegetation provides shelter for prey and predators.
peixe-cachorro.distribution: Paraguay Basin and neighboring regions of South America.
peixe-cachorro.ecologicalImportance: Regulates small fish communities in freshwater environments.

pacupeva.description: Small to medium-sized fish that explores vegetation, fruits and seeds in freshwater environments.
pacupeva.physicalCharacteristics: High and compressed body, strong teeth and silvery color.
pacupeva.habitat: Rivers, lagoons, bays and vegetated banks.
pacupeva.behavior: It explores schools and uses shallow areas during feeding periods.
pacupeva.diet: Fruits, seeds, plants, algae and small invertebrates.
curiosities: The diet follows the seasonal supply of fruits and seeds.
Flooded areas increase access to terrestrial food.
pacupeva.distribution: Basins of southern and central South America.
pacupeva.ecologicalImportance: Transfers plant matter to the aquatic chain and can disperse seeds.

abelha-jatai.description: A social stingless bee that lives in colonies and visits flowers from different environments in the Pantanal.
abelha-jatai.physicalCharacteristics: Small, dark body with yellowish markings and transparent wings.
abelha-jatai.habitat: Hollows, cavities, trunks and protected structures in vegetation areas.
abelha-jatai.behavior: It lives in colonies, collects floral resources and defends the entrance to the nest.
curiosities: The species is traditionally bred in meliponaries.
The entrance to the nest may have a characteristic cerumen structure.
abelha-jatai.distribution: Wide distribution in tropical America, including Brazil.
abelha-jatai.ecologicalImportance: Pollinates native and agricultural plants, contributing to plant regeneration.

formiga-cortadeira.description: Social ant that cuts leaves and grows fungi inside underground nests.
formiga-cortadeira.physicalCharacteristics: Castes with different sizes, strong jaws and numerous colonies.
formiga-cortadeira.habitat: Soil from fields, edges, clearings and vegetation areas.
formiga-cortadeira.behavior: It organizes trails, transports plant fragments and maintains fungi agriculture.
formiga-cortadeira.diet: Fungus cultivated with plant material collected by the colony.
curiosities: The castes share cutting, transport, defense and care tasks.
Nests alter soil structure and cycling.
formiga-cortadeira.distribution: South America, with wide occurrence in Brazilian areas.
formiga-cortadeira.ecologicalImportance: It moves plant matter and modifies the soil, influencing decomposition and nutrients.

aranha-armadeira.description: Nocturnal wandering spider that uses leaf litter, trunks and vegetation for shelter and hunting.
aranha-armadeira.physicalCharacteristics: Robust body, long legs and characteristic defensive posture when threatened.
aranha-armadeira.habitat: Leaf litter, trunks, palm trees, edges and environments with plant shelter.
aranha-armadeira.behavior: It hunts without a web at night and reacts defensively when disturbed.
curiosities: The defensive posture explains the popular name.
It must not be manipulated; Observation must keep a safe distance.
aranha-armadeira.distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions of South America.
aranha-armadeira.ecologicalImportance: Controls arthropod populations in the understory and leaf litter.
